title: Information overload, television and conflicting news
summary: He avoids television, laments contradictory media reports on masks and constant news pop-ups on computer and phone.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Do you think it’s partly because we are bombarded with so much information 24 hours a day that it stifles us?

I think that’s the point. I stopped watching television a long time ago. You know, if you ask my wife, you see now they have this new flat screen television and we have one of them. I don’t even know how to turn it on. You know there are two remotes apparently, one is for the TV and the other one is for the box. I have no idea which one is which and how it works. Really. You know, so I have to absorb a little bit of television when my wife wants to watch it. But otherwise I’m not going to turn it on. I don’t need it you know. And you know the other issue that is very important, and you know but I’m starting to get this very alarming feeling that we don’t know anymore where is the truth because you turn on one channel and they tell you one thing. You turn on the other channel, they tell you the opposite. Then you turn on the day after the same channel and they say the opposite of what they were saying the day before. And it’s been going on like this now for months. You know we know the problem with the masks. At the beginning there were people that were saying masks are useless. We shouldn’t be wearing the masks. Actually some doctors say that the mask will make you sick. Other doctors were saying no you use the mask just to prevent yourself from contaminating the environment. And so they kept going weeks with this issue of the masks. You know? So people is going to go crazy trying to decide what to do and what is right to do. You know I don’t know I think in a few years once this will be over, I hope that some scientists they will run a sort of sociological study about all this mess that happened.
Yes. I think historians and sociologists are going to be busy with 2020 for a long time.

Yeah. Because this is beyond the — you know the way that we are bombarded. But it’s not only TV. You’ve got to be careful also in the internet. Now I don’t know why, when I turn on my computer and I start the browser, right away I get a pop-up of news. So I don’t know how to turn that off you know. But even if you don’t want — my phone every morning during the day I get something that pops up and then you click, you put your finger there and you get news. And it’s just one news after the other, just bad stuff happening. You know? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
